artifacts.summary: All 7 phases completed: self-modification tie-breaker and phase-aware gating, wired into both orchestration engines, classifier test-coverage baseline, classifier maps researching/planning to real phase groups, eligibility exclusion removed with all falsified arguments re-derived, lock-aware demotion guard in reconcile-task-status.sh, and the normative guardrails record.

completion_data.completion_summary: Repaired both coupled defects in /orchestrate's multi-task admission predicate: the self-modification gate now has a deterministic designated-candidate tie-breaker and phase-aware gating (ending N-self-modifying-task deadlock and the operator 'run it solo' instruction), and eligibility is no longer status-gated on {researching, planning} (tasks stranded by a dead prior session's stale lock are admitted, classified, and dispatched instead of silently skipped forever). Every co-maintained copy and falsified safety argument was re-derived in the same phase as its mechanism; the classifier suite gained fixtures demonstrated RED against the pre-fix classifier and GREEN post-fix; a genuine regression this change caused in an existing fixture (test-conflict-predicate.sh) was found and fixed in the same phase.

memory_candidates.content: When adding an optional CLI argument that reassigns which of two ALREADY-EXISTING output shapes a caller lands in (rather than introducing a new field or shape), it does not require a schema/verdict version bump, even in a codebase with a strict version-bump-on-any-consumer-visible-change convention. The bump criterion in this codebase (see docs/architecture/batch-admit-schema.md's Version History) is specifically about a stale consumer mis-bucketing an unrecognized NEW shape into an existing branch, or silently losing a signal on a NEW field it doesn't know to look for. Neither applies when the change only shifts which existing branch a given input reaches. Document this reasoning explicitly in the version-history section rather than silently keeping the old version number, so a future reader does not assume the omission was an oversight.

In bash scripts under `set -euo pipefail`, a bare `var=$(cmd)` assignment where cmd's exit code is a ROUTINE, EXPECTED non-zero outcome (not an error) silently aborts the whole script before the exit code can ever be captured into a second variable. This bit reconcile-task-status.sh's new task-lock.sh check integration: the fix is `if var=$(cmd); then exit=0; else exit=$?; fi`, which is `-e`-exempt and preserves the real exit code. This exact pattern is already documented and used elsewhere in this codebase (orchestrate-batch-admit.sh, state-write.sh, task-lock.sh, git-commit-scoped.sh) for the same reason -- any new integration of a multi-exit-code CLI contract under set -e should default to this idiom rather than a bare assignment, and should grep for the sibling instances first to match the established style.
